utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-R77.1, the contempt case of Shefqet Kabashi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We are here today because, as it was said in the Bulatovic contempt case, a Rule 77 hearing would take place, a Rule 77 hearing to be understood as the proceedings with a purpose the same as the last stages of the pre-trial proceedings and of the trial itself in a contempt case. We see that the accused is not present, and therefore the first task for this Trial Chamber at this moment is to find out what happened. We have two possible sources at this moment to find out what happened, that is, the Victims and Witnesses Section, who may have knowledge about whereabouts of Mr. Kabashi and about recent developments and communication with him. And, Mr. Karnavas, you -- I don't know whether your assignment as Defence counsel has been completed, but at least I do understand that you act as Defence counsel for Mr. Kabashi. And within the limits of your professional obligations in relation to confidentiality, the Chamber would first like to invite you to see whether you can inform the Chamber that the first question would be whether you received a copy of the order in lieu of an indictment which serves actually as an indictment in a contempt case, in which the Chamber formulated the charges the Chamber brings against Mr. Kabashi and in which he was summoned to appear today at 9.00 in this courtroom. Could you inform the Chamber, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, good morning, Your Honours. Yes, I did receive that order. I explained to my client that I would be seeing him yesterday afternoon at approximately 3.00 because I was scheduled to be in court the day before yesterday up until 7.00 and then the following -- yesterday morning I was back in court and I was scheduled to do a rather complex cross-examination so I had indicated to him that as soon as I would get out of court I would be with him and spend several hours to go over the order, which we had anticipated, and then also to prepare for the hearing. I did go there yesterday. I arrived at approximately 3.15 or so, but when I got there somebody from the Victims and Witnesses Section was already there. She greeted me and informed me that she had arrived earlier because she also understood that I would be there at approximately 3.00 to meet with my client and wanted to be there and she had informed me that apparently his room -- there was nothing in his room other than a note. I was then later on informed of the contents of the note, and that's all the information that I have. I don't think it's revealed anything that would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have one very specific question on my mind, that's the following. When you made the appointment to meet with Mr. Kabashi yesterday at 3.00, that was the time of the appointment, did you communicate with him by telephone?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Right after the hearing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Right after the hearing --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right after the hearing I spent approximately 10 minutes with him, maybe 15, again explaining to him how we would proceed and I informed him that because of my schedule that I would be coming to see him. So we had made that arrangement at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would it be right to then assume that when you last had a communication with him that you were not aware of the summons to appear this morning at 9.00 in this courtroom and therefore you could not communicate it with him, or is this wrongly understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My understanding from the hearing, Your Honour, was that we would be back here at 9.00. So to me it was rather clear. I did not have the order. Later on I did get the order while I was in court and actually read it. I communicated to him that we would be, in fact, in court today in the morning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- and that's why I went to meet with him to prepare for the hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And did you tell him that your perception that would be to answer contempt charges, or you might not have been certain about it at that moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I -- from listening to the hearing and -- Your Honour, having followed the Bulatovic case somewhat, I was aware that he was going to be asked to provide certain information, and that's why I had the transcript with me yesterday when I went there to go over it, because I did spend approximately 30 minutes with him or 40 minutes discussing in general why he was apprehensive in answering questions, but yesterday I wanted to go into greater detail, but my understanding was that -- what I communicated to him was basically that he was going to need to give an explanation. What I did not communicate to him that the parties wouldn't be here -- well, the Prosecution, I should say, wouldn't be here. Because it was understood that there wasn't going to be a hearing with the accused but I assumed that he understood that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore he was informed also that there was a fair chance that prosecution for contempt would follow?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that information, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the Chamber would like to invite Ms. Wendy Lobwein, who is stand-by, as I understand, I understand, and who is an officer in the Victims and Witnesses Section. Mr. Karnavas, in the practice of this Chamber, officers of the Tribunal are not taking an oath when they inform the Chamber. If you would have any objection against such procedure, I would like to hear from you. If not, we'll just proceed and ask information from Ms. Lobwein.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no objection to that. I assume we're all officers of the court. At least, where I come from it doesn't matter whether you take an oath or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOBWEIN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the record you are Ms Wendy Lobwein, and you're an officer, I think even the acting chief?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOBWEIN
utterances.text: Deputy chief of the Victim and Witness Section and officer in charge at the moment while our chief's away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Lobwein, two days ago Mr. Kabashi appeared as a witness in the case against Haradinaj et al. The -- Mr. Kabashi made a solemn declaration, answered a few questions, and then we came to a point where he did not answer any further questions. The Chamber then had to consider what to do, and yesterday the Chamber issued an order in lieu of an indictment for contempt and expected Mr. Kabashi to appear here this morning at 9.00 to answer to those charges -- one charge, it was one charge and not more charges. As a witness, Mr. Kabashi was ordered to keep himself available for the Tribunal and not to leave the territory of the Netherlands. It now turns out, as we heard from Mr. Karnavas a minute ago, that Mr. Kabashi checked out of his -- at least left his hotel room empty and did not appear at the time and the place where he had made an appointment with Mr. Karnavas. I'd like to invite you to give us any further information. Mr. Karnavas told us already that when he was waiting for Mr. Kabashi, that a representative of the Victims and Witnesses Section was there as well and that a note was found in his hotel room. Could you give us further information?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOBWEIN
utterances.text: Yes. I might start from the Tuesday evening when Mr. Kabashi had returned to his hotel after court, and that evening he was seen by one of our staff. He said he was thinking of going to Germany to visit relatives, and she informed him that he couldn't travel to Germany. So that was the last time he was seen by our staff. On Wednesday morning, our staff tried to contact Mr. Kabashi from about 10.00 in the morning, and so continued to try and reach him through his mobile telephone and at the hotel until -- right through until Mr. -- appointment with Mr. Karnavas at 3.00. It was at 3.15, it was our section staff who went with the hotel staff into his room just to see if there was anything missed there or there was anything there, and that was when it was seen that his belongings had all gone and there was a note next to his bed. Since that time we've just continued to contact his mobile telephone every hour through till midnight last night and this morning but it's on an automatic redirect to an answering service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you inform us in more detail about the note that has been found in his hotel room.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOBWEIN
utterances.text: I brought the note here with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOBWEIN
utterances.text: It's two-sided in handwriting and on one side it says: "Please give these notes to the Tribunal," and our address. And the text is on the other side. And the translation done by our own staff, so not the CLSS translators -- shall I read it, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOBWEIN
utterances.text: It says: "For many reasons in this court, conditions are not fulfilled for a witness to testify properly. That's why I decided not to testify and to ask from Trial Chamber to release me from this courtroom and to give me -- and to give the right and security to go back to my family. I tell these things with full trust and conscience and stay behind this request. Thank you. If the Trial Chambers needs explanations, I can give them without hesitation." Signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Lobwein. Mr. Karnavas, I don't have to give the Prosecution an opportunity to make any submissions to the Chamber, since the Chamber as you may have learned from the order in lieu of an indictment, the Chamber itself took upon itself the task to prosecute Mr. Kabashi for -- on the charge of contempt. Nevertheless, the Chamber would like to invite you, in the assumption - that's how I understood your appearance here - that you are at least acting Defence counsel, you would take all the responsibilities for being his Defence counsel, apart from administrative arrangements perhaps still to be made or already made, but to submit to the Chamber whatever you'd like to submit in terms of how to proceed. If you want to refrain from submissions, of course you're free to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. At this point in time I think perhaps the Chamber would be best to act on its own discretion. Of course the gentleman may show up later in the day, I don't know, in which case perhaps we can have the hearing at some other point. I understand that -- at least what I had communicated to him was that we needed to be in court today. So I don't think -- I don't know whether he fully understood that, but one can draw that conclusion. I -- but I leave it to the Court's discretion, and until I'm told otherwise, I will, you know, remain as his counsel unless I'm relieved by the Court or by the Registry. So if he does show up, I'm available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. Ms. Lobwein, you have informed us -- you are not a party to these proceedings so I'm not going to ask you to making any submissions. I, however, would like to invite you, whenever you receive any information about the whereabouts of Mr. Kabashi, to inform the Chamber without delay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is not in a position to proceed against Mr. Kabashi in his absence. Trials in absentia even for contempt are not known in the rules in the Statute and the rules of the Tribunal, to the extent that evidence is heard in the absence of the accused, that would be under Rule 61. The requirements for such a hearing are not fulfilled and the Chamber does not express any opinion at this moment as to whether it would be appropriate to hear any evidence in the contempt case under Rule 61, but certainly that is not an option open to the Tribunal, to this Chamber, perhaps never but at least not at this moment. Therefore, the Chamber cannot do anything else than to adjourn sine die and consider what steps to take in order to ensure that the charge of contempt will be adjudicated. We stand adjourned sine die.
